headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Roo Code can write and execute in shared VS Code workspaces, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and cannot verify or constrain injected content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code reads and writes workspace files and can use MCP, so malicious content in shared files could influence its prompts. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and has no ingestion path, so the pairwise injection path is one-way and not universal. The shared filesystem bridge makes this plausible by default.
conditions: IF Roo Code is pointed at a workspace containing attacker-controlled instructions
IF python-cheatsheet content is copied into files that Roo Code later reads
mitigations: Restrict Roo Code to a clean workspace
Disable MCP servers for untrusted projects
Keep instruction text out of shared files
Review workspace files before opening them in Roo Code

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code can read workspace files and send content to configured model APIs or MCP servers, so sensitive data in the workspace may leave the local environment. python-cheatsheet does not read files or handle secrets, so it is not a leakage source, but it also cannot prevent exposure once Roo Code ingests shared files.
conditions: IF sensitive source code or secrets are present in the VS Code workspace
IF Roo Code is configured with a remote model API or MCP server
mitigations: Open Roo Code in a scrubbed copy of the project
Audit MCP server access before enabling it

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has broad write, shell, git, and filesystem access in a shared VS Code workspace, while python-cheatsheet is non-runnable and cannot coordinate or lock state. The overlap is asymmetric but still dangerous because Roo Code can mutate shared files without any locking mechanism from the other agent, creating direct write conflicts and git-state races.
conditions: IF Roo Code and any other instance touch the same workspace files
IF git state is modified while multiple instances are active
mitigations: Pause one agent before the other writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on workspace content and browser screenshots, so if it treats python-cheatsheet-derived text as authoritative, errors can propagate into edits or actions. python-cheatsheet itself does not execute actions, which lowers blast radius, but the pair still supports a default path where unverified content is reused downstream.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses text from python-cheatsheet as source material without verification
IF Roo Code then applies that text to code edits, shell commands, or browser actions
mitigations: Require a verification step before acting on copied text
Use citations or source links in downstream tasks

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for python-cheatsheet, and Roo Code’s docs only show general workspace and model-API handling. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is undocumented and the other agent has no data handling surface, only a small residual compliance risk remains.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Roo Code’s workspace
IF the configured model provider or MCP server has stricter retention than the operator expects
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Use a local model for sensitive tasks
